hunt.justification: Adversaries are using legitimate remote-support tools to bypass security boundaries and expand laterally using native protocols like WinRM. This hunt protects the critical internal infrastructure that these multi-stage paths target.

meta.name: IT Support Impersonation and WinRM Lateral Expansion

related.reason: The initial impersonation via Teams is an identity-focused hunt that precedes the endpoint activities covered here.

meta.analysis: A single rule on Node.js execution might be too noisy in developer environments; this hunt correlates the rare runtime with preceding remote-support takeover and following lateral movement, providing the full context an analyst needs to act.

coverage.reason: AD mapping via WinRM typically uses internal API calls or LDAP traffic not captured in standard process or network activity surfaces.
Not examined by this hunt; belongs to a separate hunt.

scenario.summary: Attackers impersonate IT support via Microsoft Teams to trick users into granting control via legitimate remote-support software, followed by the deployment of a portable Node.js runtime for command-and-control. Once established, the operators map Active Directory and move laterally to critical infrastructure like domain controllers and certificate authorities using WinRM.

meta.rationale: Focus on endpoints where remote-support software is prevalent but restricted to IT use. Provide known Domain Controller and CA IP addresses to refine the lateral movement detection.
meta.hypothesis: An adversary has hijacked a remote-support session to execute PowerShell, use a portable Node.js runtime for C2, and expand laterally via WinRM to domain controllers.

blind_spots.risk: While the connection is visible, the impact (e.g., AD mapping, account creation) remains hidden without detailed host logs on the destination.
blind_spots.question: Which specific administrative commands were executed on the Domain Controller?
blind_spots.requires: WinRM Operational logging or deep packet inspection
blind_spots.remediation: Enable WinRM auditing and Process Command Line logging on all Domain Controllers and Certificate Authorities.

blind_spots.risk: If node.exe is renamed to svchost.exe or similar, the current process_name filter will miss it.
blind_spots.question: Did the attacker rename the portable Node.js runtime to masquerade as a system process?
blind_spots.requires: hb_process_activity with original file name or hash-based detection
blind_spots.remediation: Deploy hash-based monitoring for known portable runtimes or utilize original_file_name columns in process activity queries.

hunt.name: IT Support Impersonation and WinRM Lateral Expansion
hunt.description: This hunt identifies the multi-stage progression of the CaptiveCrunch campaign. It first isolates hosts where legitimate remote-support tools are used as a launchpad for PowerShell-based MSI downloads. It then pivots to find the deployment of rare Node.js runtimes in user-writable paths and subsequent WinRM connections to sensitive internal infrastructure like Domain Controllers and Certificate Authorities.

nodes.label: Inventory of hosts with remote support software

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, package_name, package_version, install_path FROM hb_software_inventory WHERE (LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%anydesk%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%teamviewer%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%connectwise%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%screenconnect%' OR LOWER(package_name) LIKE '%quick assist%') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0)
config.description: Find the subset of the estate where remote support tools are installed to focus behavioral analysis.
config.expected_signal: A list of hosts with known remote-support packages. Silence is expected if these tools are not in the official inventory.

nodes.label: Remote support tools spawning administrative shells

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, time, process_name, process_cmd_line, parent_process_name, user_name FROM hb_process_activity WHERE instr(',' || '{{remote_support_tool_names}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(parent_process_name) || ',') > 0 AND instr(',' || '{{admin_shell_binaries}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(process_name) || ',') > 0 AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0)
config.description: Identify process patterns where a support tool acts as a parent to a shell or installer.
config.expected_signal: A support tool launching PowerShell, CMD, or MSIExec. Legitimate admin use may occur but will be weighed by the agent.

nodes.label: PowerShell script blocks downloading MSI files

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, time, script_content, actor_user_name FROM hb_script_activity WHERE LOWER(script_content) LIKE '%.msi%' AND (LOWER(script_content) LIKE '%download%' OR LOWER(script_content) LIKE '%iwr%' OR LOWER(script_content) LIKE '%http%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0)
config.description: Detect the specific scripting commands used to retrieve malicious installer packages.
config.expected_signal: Script contents showing network-based retrieval of MSI files. This is a behavioral indicator of staging.

config.objective: Identify hosts where remote support software spawned PowerShell or MSIExec to download external packages.
config.description: Assess whether the remote tool execution and subsequent scripting indicate a compromise on specific hosts.
config.expected_signal: Identification of hosts with high-confidence takeover activity.
config.success_criteria: A per-host verdict citing the specific process and script rows that indicate malicious staging.

nodes.label: Prevalence of Node.js runtimes in user paths

config.content: SELECT LOWER(process_path) AS path, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS hosts, COUNT(*) AS runs, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_process_activity WHERE LOWER(process_name) = 'node.exe' AND (LOWER(process_path) LIKE '%\users\%' OR LOWER(process_path) LIKE '%\public\%' OR LOWER(process_path) LIKE '%\temp\%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) GROUP BY 1 HAVING hosts <= 5 ORDER BY hosts ASC
config.description: Stack-count Node.js executions from user-writable paths to isolate the portable C2 runtime from official installations.
config.expected_signal: A Node.js binary seen on only a few hosts, running from a non-standard directory. Common developer installs will appear across more hosts.

primitive_config.label: Prevalence of Node.js runtimes in user paths
primitive_config.content: SELECT LOWER(process_path) AS path, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS hosts, COUNT(*) AS runs, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_process_activity WHERE LOWER(process_name) = 'node.exe' AND (LOWER(process_path) LIKE '%\users\%' OR LOWER(process_path) LIKE '%\public\%' OR LOWER(process_path) LIKE '%\temp\%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) GROUP BY 1 HAVING hosts <= 5 ORDER BY hosts ASC
primitive_config.expected: A Node.js binary seen on only a few hosts, running from a non-standard directory. Common developer installs will appear across more hosts.

nodes.label: WinRM connections to sensitive internal targets

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, time, process_name, dst_endpoint_ip, dst_endpoint_port, direction FROM hb_network_connection WHERE (dst_endpoint_port IN (5985, 5986) OR LOWER(process_name) = 'wsmprovhost.exe') AND (instr(',' || '{{sensitive_ip_targets}}' || ',', ',' || dst_endpoint_ip || ',') > 0 OR '{{sensitive_ip_targets}}' = '') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0)
config.description: Identify lateral movement attempts targeting high-value infrastructure like Domain Controllers.
config.expected_signal: Connections from the suspected beachhead to sensitive IPs over WinRM ports. Silence means no such connections were logged.

config.objective: Determine if any host identified as suspicious in the early triage also displays rare Node.js runtimes and WinRM lateral movement.
config.description: Connect the early takeover evidence with the follow-on portable runtime and WinRM activity to confirm the full attack path.
config.expected_signal: A high-fidelity verdict for hosts that display the complete progression from takeover to expansion.
config.success_criteria: A final verdict of malicious for hosts matching the CaptiveCrunch behavioral pattern.

config.question: the final triage verdict is malicious for at least one host, linking remote-support takeover to lateral movement
config.condition: the final triage verdict is malicious for at least one host, linking remote-support takeover to lateral movement
config.description: Direct confirmed malicious activity to isolation and analyst review.
Prevent further lateral movement or data exfiltration by isolating the confirmed beachhead.
config.instructions: Isolate the host identified in the triage verdict. Revoke any active sessions for the user(s) associated with the remote-support takeover.

config.description: Manually verify the scope of the lateral expansion on the Domain Controller side.
config.instructions: Review WinRM logs (Event ID 91) on the targeted Domain Controllers to identify executed commands. Search for any new MSI installations or portable node.exe binaries on those systems.

config.description: Finalize the investigation and document findings.
config.instructions: Record the hosts examined and the final verdicts. If legitimate remote support was found but used as a vector, recommend tighter ASR rules.
